name: Ultimate
energy: Repeated sprints and cuts on a high aerobic base: heart rate averages about 82% of max, and sprint output drops late in each half.
summary: Ultimate is repeated sprints, hard cuts and jumps to catch, with knee, thigh and ankle injuries most common. The plan builds leg strength, speed and repeat-sprint fitness, and adds landing, hamstring, ankle and shoulder work.

evidence.claim: Male players covered about 4.7 km a game with 17 sprints, averaged 82% of max heart rate, and did 43-47% less high-intensity running late in each half.
evidence.source: Krustrup & Mohr 2015, Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research

evidence.claim: The lower limb is most often injured, mainly the knee and thigh; muscle strains and joint sprains are the most common types.
Neuromuscular injury-prevention programmes cut ACL injuries by about 50% overall and non-contact ACL injuries in female athletes by about 67%.
evidence.source: Webster & Hewett 2018, Journal of Orthopaedic Research

variants.name: Cutter
variants.desc: Most repeated sprints, deep cuts, high catches and layouts.
variants.note: Your plan adds extra Nordic curls and keeps sprint and repeat-sprint work at the top of the week.

variants.name: Handler
variants.desc: Shorter bursts, pivots and marking, with far more throws.
variants.note: Your plan adds forearm and rotation work for throwing volume. Keep 10 min of easy throws in every warm-up.

variants.name: Beach
variants.desc: Sand cuts impact but costs about 1.2-1.6 times the energy of grass running, with lower jumps.
variants.note: Your plan adds extra calf work for sand. Build sand running time over 2-3 weeks before a beach event.

slots.note: Heavy but fast, never to failure

in.name: Short primer
in.focus: Midweek top-up if you have a free day

off.name: Aerobic base
off.intensity: 85-95% max heart rate, hard but steady
off.why: Average heart rate in a game is about 82% of max, so the aerobic base sets how well you recover between points.

off.name: Tempo runs
off.why: Builds running volume and tissue tolerance before faster work.

pre.name: Repeat sprints with cuts
pre.work: 2-3 sets of 6 x 20-30 m with a 90 degree cut
pre.rest: 20-25 s between sprints, 4 min between sets
pre.why: Sprint output drops late in each half; this trains you to repeat it.

pre.name: 15 s on, 15 s off
pre.why: Raises aerobic power for point after point.

pre.name: Top speed exposure
pre.why: Regular near-max sprinting helps protect the hamstrings.

pre.name: Sand running
pre.why: Sand costs more energy and loads the calves differently, so build it up before beach events.

in.name: Top-up sprints
in.work: 6 x 20 m plus 3 x 30 m build-ups
in.why: For weeks with no game or little playing time.

tests.name: 10 m sprint
tests.how: Start 0.5 m behind the line, phone slow-motion video, best of 3.
tests.note: Women about 0.1-0.15 s slower. Bands are a coaching guide.

tests.name: Countermovement jump
tests.how: Hands on hips, jump app or jump mat, best of 3.
tests.note: Youth national team selection cut-off was about 40.5 cm. Women about 20% lower.

tests.name: Yo-Yo intermittent recovery level 1
tests.how: 20 m shuttles to beeps with 10 s jog recovery, until you miss two beeps.
tests.note: Moderately trained men averaged about 1790 m. Women about 30% lower.

tests.name: 505 change of direction
tests.how: 10 m run-in, time the 5 m to the line, 180 degree turn and 5 m back. Both sides.
tests.note: Compare left and right turns. Bands are a coaching guide.

tests.name: Single-leg hop for distance
tests.how: Hop and stick on one leg, best of 3 each side.
tests.note: A gap above 10-15% between legs is a flag to work on.

week: Game Saturday, training Tue and Thu: heavy lower on Monday or Wednesday, at least 72 h before the first game.
Upper body and rotation can go 2 days before.
Day before a tournament: rest or a 15 min primer only.
Day after a tournament weekend: walk, bike or swim 20-30 min, mobility.
No heavy lower work within 48 h after a 2-day tournament.
primer: 3 x 20 m sprints with a cut
Easy throws, building up to full power

lines: Last heavy lower session 5-7 days before the event.
Cut gym sets by about half; keep the weights heavy.
Between games: eat and drink after every game, keep moving, stay out of the sun.

rules: No heavy lower or high-volume jumps within 72 h before a game or tournament.
Nordic curls stay in all year, at least 1 set a week in season.
Players with a past ankle sprain: brace or tape for games.
Build sand running gradually before beach events.
